title: Impersonal 4: Пора and Timing (it is time to)
description: Пора announces that the moment for an action has arrived: Пора идти. With a verb of motion, the infinitive is often dropped and only the destination remains: Маше пора домой. Optional dative names whose moment it is.
descriptionRussian: «Пора» объявляет, что наступило время для действия: «Пора идти». С глаголом движения инфинитив часто опускается, и остаётся только направление: «Маше пора домой». Дательный падеж (по желанию) называет, чьё это время.
intro: One word, one meaning, and a neat shortcut. Normally an infinitive follows, but if the verb would be a motion verb and you name where you are going, Russian drops the verb entirely and leaves just the destination. Time for school, with no going in the sentence at all.
rules: Пора means 'it is time to.' The pattern is (dative, optional) + пора + infinitive: Пора идти, Нам пора начинать.
The dative names whose moment it is: Маше пора вставать. With no dative the timing is general: Пора обедать.
When the verb is a verb of motion AND a destination is named, drop the infinitive and keep only the destination: Маше пора домой (not пора идти домой).
Past adds было, future adds будет, placed beside пора and never changing form: пора было уходить, скоро будет пора. The usual order in the past is пора было.
Не пора is rare; to say the moment has not arrived, say ещё не пора ('not time yet').
examples: Пора идти, уже поздно. (It is time to go, it is already late.) General timing; imperfective infinitive идти.
Маше пора вставать. (It is time for Masha to get up.) Dative Маше names whose moment it is.
Антону пора домой. (It is time for Anton to head home.) Motion verb dropped; destination домой remains.
Нам пора на работу. (It is time for us to go to work.) Dative нам + destination на работу, no infinitive.
Уже пора было уходить. (It was already time to leave.) Past tense with было beside пора.
Ещё не пора, посиди немного. (It is not time yet, sit a while.) The standard negation ещё не пора.

tables.title: Пора: full infinitive vs dropped-infinitive pattern

rows.label: Ordinary verb
cells: Infinitive stays: not a motion verb.

rows.label: Motion verb + destination
cells: Infinitive DROPS: destination implies the motion.

rows.label: Motion verb + destination + dative
cells: Dative names the person; infinitive still drops.

items.promptEnglish: It is already late, it is time to go home.
items.hint: Which word announces that the moment has arrived?
items.explanation: Пора announces timing ('the moment has come'), reinforced by 'уже поздно.' Стоит would mean 'it is worth going home' (value advice), лучше would mean 'had better' (mild urgency), and нельзя is a prohibition. Only пора names the arrival of the moment.

items.prompt: Маше пора _____, иначе она опоздает на поезд.
items.promptEnglish: It is time for Masha to head home, otherwise she will miss the train.
items.hint: After пора with a motion verb and a destination, the infinitive drops.
items.explanation: With пора, a motion verb plus a named destination drops the infinitive: Маше пора домой. 'Идти домой' and 'пойти домой' keep an infinitive that everyday Russian leaves out here. 'Дома' (at home, prepositional) names location, not direction, so it cannot follow пора.

items.promptEnglish: It is time to eat lunch, it is already one o'clock.
items.hint: The clock cue points to timing, not advice.
items.explanation: The time cue 'уже час дня' signals that the moment has arrived, which is пора. Стоит would mean 'it is worth eating lunch,' хочется is a personal feeling ('I feel like'), and можно is permission ('one may'). The clock makes it timing.

items.promptEnglish: It is time for Anton to head to work, the workday is starting.
items.hint: A destination after пора shows direction of motion (accusative).
items.explanation: The dropped-infinitive пора pattern needs a direction-of-motion phrase: на работу (to work, accusative). 'На работе' is the prepositional ('at work', location), 'работа' is the bare nominative, and 'о работе' means 'about work.' Only на работу shows movement toward a destination.

items.promptEnglish: It is time for Masha to head home - it is already dark.
items.hint: The dropped-infinitive пора pattern: which direction word?
items.explanation: With пора and an implied motion verb, the destination stands in its direction form: пора домой. Дома ('at home') and в доме are locations, not directions; до дома would need the full verb.

items.promptEnglish: It was already time for us to leave when the rain started.
items.hint: Past timing: which frozen form joins пора?
items.explanation: Past timing adds the frozen neuter было: нам было пора уходить. Была would wrongly agree; impersonal constructions have no subject to agree with. Будет is the future.

items.promptEnglish: It is time for Anton to head to work - the workday is starting.
items.hint: Naming a destination lets пора drop the verb. Which case?
items.explanation: The dropped-infinitive пора needs a direction phrase in the accusative: пора на работу. На работе is the location ('at work'), which cannot express heading somewhere.

blanks: Нам уже _____ домой, концерт закончился. (It is time for us to head home, the concert is over.)
_____ спать, завтра рано вставать. (It is time to sleep, we have to get up early tomorrow.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Both blanks announce that the moment has arrived, which is пора. In the first, the motion verb is dropped and only the destination домой remains (нам пора домой). Стоит would say 'it is worth going,' лучше 'had better,' and нельзя is a prohibition - none names timing.

sentenceBuilding.translation: It is time for Masha to head home.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Motion verb dropped: dative + пора + destination.

sentenceBuilding.translation: It is time for us to go, it is already late.
sentenceBuilding.hint: No destination named, so the motion infinitive идти stays.

sentenceBuilding.translation: It is time for Anton to head to work.
sentenceBuilding.hint: Destination на работу (accusative); drop the infinitive.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: It is late, it is time for Anton to head home.
errorCorrection.explanation: Only пора can drop the infinitive when a motion verb is implied and a destination is named: Антону пора домой. Стоит, следует, and лучше all require a spoken infinitive (Антону стоит пойти домой), so 'Антону стоит домой' is incomplete. The cue 'уже поздно' also points to timing, which is пора.

errorCorrection.sentence: Детям пора в школе, уже восемь утра.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: It is time for the children to head to school; it is already eight.
errorCorrection.explanation: The dropped-infinitive пора pattern needs a direction-of-motion phrase in the accusative: в школу. 'В школе' is the prepositional ('at school', location), which cannot show movement toward a place. Пора + destination always points, never sits.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: It is time for Masha to head home, the train is in an hour.
minimalPairs.explanation: Домой (homeward) shows direction of motion, which the dropped-infinitive пора pattern requires. Дома means 'at home' (location), and пора with a dropped motion verb needs a destination you move toward, not a place you already are.

minimalPairs.context: Уже пора _____ уходить, но мы остались.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: It was already time to leave, but we stayed.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'Но мы остались' is past, so the timing word is past too: пора было уходить. Будет would make it future ('it will be time'), which the past clause rules out.

reviewVocab.definition: it is time to (do); announces that the moment has arrived; takes an optional dative naming whose moment it is
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Пора идти' слово 'пора' объявляет, что наступило время уходить.

reviewVocab.definition: with a verb of motion and a named destination, the infinitive drops and only the destination stays: пора домой, пора на работу
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Маше пора домой' инфинитив 'идти' опущен, осталось только направление 'домой'.

reviewVocab.definition: past and future of пора; было for past, будет for future, both fixed forms that never change for gender or number
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Уже пора было уходить' слово 'было' ставит время в прошлое.

reviewVocab.definition: not time yet; the standard way to say the moment has not arrived (plain не пора is rare)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Ещё не пора, посиди немного' говорящий сообщает, что момент ещё не наступил.
